items.text: The system shall support discovery of books through homepage browsing sections and category navigation.

claims.claim: The homepage presents browsing sections with book listings and promotional discovery areas.
The homepage provides category navigation for browsing books.

items.evidence_note: Step 1 shows homepage browsing areas, bestseller/new release sections, category links, and language/category navigation.
items.rationale: The visible homepage supports both discovery through browsing sections and navigation-based discovery.

items.text: The system shall provide a dedicated advanced search workflow for finding books using structured search criteria.

claims.claim: The site provides an entry point to advanced search.
The advanced search page presents a dedicated structured search form.

items.evidence_note: Step 1 shows an Advanced Search button; step 2 shows the Advanced Search page with structured fields.
items.rationale: The flow visibly moves from the storefront to a dedicated advanced search form.

items.text: The system shall allow users to search for books using multiple bibliographic fields, including keyword, title, author, publisher, and ISBN.

claims.claim: The advanced search form exposes multiple bibliographic fields.
The visible bibliographic fields include keyword, title, author, publisher, and ISBN.

items.evidence_note: Step 2 visibly labels fields for Keyword, Title, Author, Publisher, and ISBN.
items.rationale: All named fields in the requirement are visible in the advanced search form.

items.text: The system shall allow users to constrain advanced search by language.

claims.claim: The advanced search form includes a language criterion.
A specific language can be selected in the advanced search form.

items.evidence_note: Step 2 shows a Language selector; step 4 shows it set to German.
items.rationale: The form visibly supports constraining the advanced search by language.

items.text: The system shall provide an explicit action to submit configured advanced search criteria.

claims.claim: The advanced search form provides a clearly labeled Search action.

items.evidence_note: A Search button is visible on the advanced search page before and after criteria are configured.
items.rationale: The requirement asks for a submission mechanism, and the visible Search button satisfies that observable mechanism.

items.text: The system shall keep configured advanced search criteria visibly reflected in the search form before submission.

claims.claim: The entered author criterion remains visible in the form before submission.
The selected language criterion remains visible in the form before submission.

items.evidence_note: Step 3 shows Author set to Stephen King; step 4 still shows Stephen King and shows Language set to German.
items.rationale: Configured criteria are visibly reflected in the form state before any results page is shown.

items.text: The system shall display books matching the submitted advanced search filters so the user can browse filtered results.
items.annotation_notes: The visible setup is supported, but the required filtered browsing outcome is not shown and result correctness cannot be verified from the screenshots.

claims.claim: The user can configure advanced search filters for author and language.
The system displays a browsing view of books after the configured advanced search is submitted.
The displayed books actually match all submitted filters.

items.evidence_note: The screenshots show filter configuration and a Search button, but no submitted results page.
items.rationale: The visible setup is supported, but the required filtered browsing outcome is not shown and result correctness cannot be verified from the screenshots.

items.text: The system shall preserve global storefront context such as account access, order status, wishlist, cart, and locale controls while the user performs search tasks.

claims.claim: Global storefront controls remain available during homepage and advanced search use.
The preserved controls include account, order status, wishlist, cart, and locale-related controls.

items.evidence_note: The header remains visible across the flow with Order Status, Wishlist, My Account, cart, language, and currency controls.
items.rationale: The search workflow preserves the visible storefront context throughout the shown steps.

items.text: The system shall support user-selectable locale settings relevant to shopping, including interface language and currency, alongside product discovery features.
items.annotation_notes: Language and currency controls are visible in the shared header across the flow, which grounds a storefront capability for locale-related preferences while searching or browsing.

claims.claim: The storefront exposes interface language and currency controls.
Locale controls are available alongside product discovery or search features.

items.evidence_note: The header shows English and $ USD controls while browsing and while using advanced search.
items.rationale: The visible dropdown-style language and currency controls support the locale selection mechanism in the shopping context.

items.text: The system shall carry active advanced search filters forward into subsequent browsing views so users can understand the basis of the shown results.
items.annotation_notes: The flow emphasizes explicit configuration of author and language before search, making it a disciplined and nearby inference that those active filters should remain understandable when results are shown, even though the results page is not visible here.

claims.claim: Active advanced search filters are reflected before submission.
A subsequent browsing or results view shows the active filters after search.

items.evidence_note: The configured filters are visible in the form, but no subsequent browsing or results view is shown.
items.rationale: Only the pre-submission filter visibility is supported; carrying filters forward into later browsing views is not evidenced.

items.text: The system shall allow users to search for books by author name within the advanced search workflow.

claims.claim: The advanced search workflow supports author-name book search.
An author name can be configured within the advanced search workflow.

items.evidence_note: Step 2 shows the author criterion, and steps 3 and 4 show it filled with an author name.
items.rationale: The visible workflow supports searching by author name in advanced search.

items.text: The system shall allow users to combine multiple advanced search criteria in a single search request, including author and language together.

claims.claim: Multiple advanced search criteria can be combined together.
Author and language criteria can be combined together in a single search request.
The combined criteria can be submitted as one search request.

items.evidence_note: Step 4 shows author and language criteria configured together with one Search action. The actual request construction is a routine internal dependency behind the visible mechanism.
items.rationale: The visible workflow supports combined criteria configuration; request construction is outside the visible verification target for this mechanism claim.

items.text: The system shall retain previously entered advanced search criteria when the user returns from a filtered browsing view to the advanced search workflow during the same session.
items.annotation_notes: The screenshots support short-term visible retention in the form, but not the stronger return-from-results persistence scenario.

claims.claim: The system retains previously entered advanced search criteria when the user returns from a filtered browsing view to the advanced search workflow during the same session.
claims.note: It is not shown, but a trivial frontend property.

items.evidence_note: The form retains visible criteria before submission, but no results view or return-to-search step is shown.
items.rationale: The screenshots support short-term visible retention in the form, but not the stronger return-from-results persistence scenario.

items.text: The system shall remember a signed-in user's preferred storefront locale and language-related search context for later visits to the search workflow.

claims.claim: The system supports storefront locale context for a signed-in user.
The system supports language-related search context.
The system remembers the preferred storefront locale and language-related search context for later visits.

items.evidence_note: The screenshots show account-related context, locale controls, and a configured language criterion, but no later visit or persisted preference state is shown.
items.rationale: Visible context is supported, while later-visit memory depends on hidden persistence outside the screenshot flow.

items.text: The system shall ensure that books shown after advanced search satisfy all submitted visible constraints, including the selected author and language.

claims.claim: Author and language constraints can be configured in advanced search.
Books are displayed after advanced search is submitted.
All shown books satisfy the selected author and language constraints.

items.evidence_note: The configured constraints are visible, but no resulting books are shown and correctness of all returned items cannot be checked.
items.rationale: The central result-correctness claim cannot be reliably judged from the provided screenshots.

items.text: The system shall include all currently available catalog titles that match the configured author and German-language criteria in the resulting browsing view.

claims.claim: Author and German-language criteria can be configured before a resulting browsing view.
A resulting browsing view is displayed after the configured criteria are submitted.
The resulting browsing view includes all currently available catalog titles that match the configured criteria.

items.evidence_note: The configured criteria are visible, but no result list is shown and catalog completeness cannot be verified from screenshots.
items.rationale: The universal completeness requirement depends on unavailable catalog state and an unshown results view.

items.text: The system shall provide a dedicated review state before executing advanced search in which the configured bibliographic and language criteria can be checked, edited, or cleared.

claims.claim: The system provides a dedicated review state before executing advanced search.
The configured criteria can be checked and edited in the visible advanced search form.
The dedicated review state provides a visible way to clear criteria.

items.evidence_note: Steps 2 to 4 show the normal advanced search form with a direct Search button, not a separate review state or clear-control review step.
items.rationale: The visible flow supports direct form editing and submission, but contradicts the presence of a dedicated review state in the shown pre-execution workflow.

items.text: The system shall expose active author and language filters in the results view as inline, directly editable controls so users can refine the search without reopening the full advanced search form.

claims.claim: Active author and language filters are established before a results view.
The results view exposes active author and language filters.
The results view exposes those filters as inline, directly editable controls.
Users can refine the search without reopening the full advanced search form.

items.evidence_note: The full advanced search state shows active author and language criteria, but no results view is included.
items.rationale: Because the results view is absent, the requested inline editable results-level filters cannot be reliably judged.
